ANONG BAHA ANG DAPAT LUMUNOD SA MGA KURAKOT?

Hindi tanaw sa toreng garing ng mga naghahari-harian ang kalunos-lunos na kalagayan ng mga Pilipinong nag-aagaw-buhay sa banta ng nagtataasang tubig-baha at tahasang kawalang-pananagutan.

Kasabay ng paggunita sa ika-53 taon mula nang ideklara ng diktador na si Marcos Sr. ang Batas Militar, sumiklab sa Luneta nitong Setyembre 21 ang malawakang kilos-protesta ng nagngangalit na taumbayan laban sa sala-salabat na katiwaliang nakaugat sa sistematikong pamamasista ng rehimeng Marcos-Duterte.

Kinapanayam ng The Manila Collegian ang iba’t ibang sektor na humanay sa pagkilos upang sinsinin ang kanilang daing sa mga korap na opisyal ng gobyerno. Anila, ang pagtindig sa Bagumbayan ay hakbang lamang sa mas marami pang laban patungo sa ganap na tagumpay.

Panayam nina Marlo Gordoncillo, Clarisse Musni, Chris John Resquid, at Carl Andrew Valois

Mga larawan nina Izabella Gabrielle Actub, Laird Ilaya, at Yaghi Parilla

data.text:
A bronze rosette was added to @USArmy Capt. Willibald Bianchi’s name on the Walls of the Missing at Manila American Cemetery Friday signifying he has been identified by @dodpaa.

The Medal of Honor recipient, missing since 1945, was honored with the nation’s highest military award for valor in 1942 for his heroism under fire, but was also remembered for his care of fellow service members during the Bataan Death March and later as a prisoner of war.

Bianchi is one of almost 120 Medal of Honor recipients buried or memorialized at American Battle Monuments Commission sites around the world. He will be the 11th of those missing in action or buried at sea to be identified with a rosette.
 
The rosette, a symbol of eternity, is crafted as a bronze rosemary wreath—a timeless emblem of honor and victory. Encircled by the eight-points of a compass, it signifies America’s commitment, reaching out in all directions to recover their remains from the farthest corners of the earth.

The end of the protest does not mark the end of our fight against corruption, demand for accountability, and thirst for transparency.

Our online and on ground presence are the keys to enacting change in the corrupt system that the Filipino people have long-endured. 

Whether it be on the streets of Manila, your own towns and provinces, or through social media: our collective involvement in this movement has caused a lasting impact. 

Let the outcome of yesterday’s protest prompt us to use this voice, these feelings, and this anger as catalysts to good governance.

The nationwide protest is but a single reminder of how powerful our voices are when we take a stand. 

We continue our calls for justice to all those who were unfairly surveilled and were victims of aggression during the protest. 

We continue our calls for fair representation and truthful reportage in the media.

We continue our calls until the Filipino people are served with the good governance we deserve. 

Let us continue to uphold our responsibility as citizens to keep ourselves informed, standing firm and consistent in our calls to truth, justice, and transparency.

And let our history and protests be a reminder of how important our right to vote is.

Kinapanayam ng The Manila Collegian ang iba’t ibang sektor na humanay sa pagkilos upang sinsinin ang kanilang daing sa mga korap na opisyal ng gobyerno. Anila, ang pagtindig sa Bagumbayan ay hakbang lamang sa mas marami pang laban patungo sa ganap na tagumpay.

Panayam nina Marlo Gordoncillo, Clarisse Musni, Chris John Resquid, at Carl Andrew Valois

Mga larawan nina Izabella Gabrielle Actub, Laird Ilaya, at Yaghi Parilla

The Philippine National Police (PNP) said on Monday that none of its personnel fired a gun or used tear gas during the protests at Mendiola on Sunday.

“Wala, hindi natin gagawin ‘yun at kung sana mayroong nangyari, may report na tayo na may ganyang incident,” said Manila Police District (MPD) spokesperson Police Major Philipp Ines on Chino Gaston's report on "24 Oras."  

A video went viral online wherein some members of MPD’s Special Weapons and Tactics team allegedly pointed a gun at a protester wearing a black shirt. 

There is also a video making the rounds on the Internet showing a person with a bleeding head lying on the ground.   For its part, the MPD said that the PNP has yet to receive a report about a police shooting or a protester who died in the rally.

ICYMI: A total of 113 people have been arrested for throwing rocks, destroying properties, and burning tires during protest action against corruption on Sunday while 93 police personnel were injured.

The Manila Police District said 51 individuals were arrested in Ayala Bridge, of which 38 were adults, two minors who were turned over to Manila Reception and Action Center, and 11 minors who were subject for determination of discernment.

It added 21 were arrested in Mendiola, 14 of which were adults and seven were minors, and 41 in Recto, 13 of which were adults and 28 minors.
